classification.difficultyReason: Read the intervals where supplied quadratic graphs lie below the x-axis, distinguishing interior and exterior intervals and excluding the roots.

inlines.text: In each of the following, the graph of
is shown. State the value(s) of

spec.sourceRegion: Concept check 1–4, upper-left graph, printed question 1.
spec.description: Upward-opening blue parabola with roots −1 and 1, an unlabelled minimum on the y-axis, and arrowheads on both branches. Black axes have positive-direction arrowheads and x and y labels. Root labels are above the x-axis. There are no grid lines, endpoint circles, origin label or shaded regions.
spec.mathematics: The roots are exactly −1 and 1 and the leading coefficient is positive. The plot uses a normalised vertical drawing coordinate to preserve the schematic shape; it does not assert a leading coefficient, vertex ordinate or numerical y-scale.
spec.answerVisibility: The complete supplied graph is visible in the question. No solution interval is highlighted.

answer.worked: The curve lies below the $x$-axis between $-1$ and $1$. The roots are excluded because $f(x)<0$ is strict. Hence, $-1<x<1$.

spec.sourceRegion: Concept check 1–4, upper-right graph, printed question 2.
spec.description: Downward-opening blue parabola with roots −2 and 2, an unlabelled maximum on the y-axis, and arrowheads on both downward branches. Black axes have positive-direction arrowheads and x and y labels. Root labels are below the x-axis. There are no grid lines, endpoint circles, origin label or shaded regions.
spec.mathematics: The roots are exactly −2 and 2 and the leading coefficient is negative. The normalised vertical coordinate represents the source's unspecified vertical scale without adding a numerical maximum or function equation.
spec.answerVisibility: The complete supplied graph is visible in the question. No solution interval is highlighted.

answer.worked: The curve lies below the $x$-axis to the left of $-2$ and to the right of $2$. The roots are excluded because the inequality is strict. Hence, $x<-2$ or $x>2$.

spec.sourceRegion: Concept check 1–4, lower-left graph, printed question 3.
spec.description: Upward-opening blue parabola with roots −1 and 2. Its unlabelled minimum is below the x-axis and to the right of the y-axis, and its y-intercept is negative. Both upward branches carry arrowheads. Black axes have positive-direction arrowheads and x and y labels. Root labels are above the x-axis. There are no grid lines, endpoint circles, origin label or shaded regions.
spec.mathematics: The roots are exactly −1 and 2 and the leading coefficient is positive. Symmetry places the minimum halfway between the roots. The vertical drawing coordinate is normalised and supplies no numerical y-value or leading coefficient.
spec.answerVisibility: The complete supplied graph is visible in the question. No solution interval is highlighted.

answer.worked: The curve lies below the $x$-axis between $-1$ and $2$. The roots are excluded because $f(x)<0$ is strict. Hence, $-1<x<2$.

spec.sourceRegion: Concept check 1–4, lower-right graph, printed question 4.
spec.description: Downward-opening blue parabola with roots −3 and 1. Its unlabelled maximum is above the x-axis and to the left of the y-axis, and its y-intercept is positive. Both downward branches carry arrowheads. Black axes have positive-direction arrowheads and x and y labels. Root labels are below the x-axis. There are no grid lines, endpoint circles, origin label or shaded regions.
spec.mathematics: The roots are exactly −3 and 1 and the leading coefficient is negative. Symmetry places the maximum halfway between the roots. The vertical drawing coordinate is normalised and supplies no numerical maximum or leading coefficient.
spec.answerVisibility: The complete supplied graph is visible in the question. No solution interval is highlighted.

answer.worked: The curve lies below the $x$-axis to the left of $-3$ and to the right of $1$. The roots are excluded because the inequality is strict. Hence, $x<-3$ or $x>1$.
